# Research handoff — use only the fields needed for this question

An existing report or pasted result is sufficient. Do not rewrite it to fill this
outline. Preserve detailed proofs and counterexamples; shorten repeated metadata,
not the mathematical argument. Routine fixes need no research handoff.

## To the researcher
Question and decision; available repository revision and scope; relevant claims,
known counterexamples, compatible results and precise source links. State any
local-only evidence the researcher cannot access. Do not attach a generic reading
curriculum or dump raw catalogues. The researcher reads deeper when needed.

## Back to Codex
State the recommendation and uncertainty. For each material new finding, preserve
its proposition, preconditions, argument, evidence and attempted falsification.
Distinguish native facts, external theory, synthetic calculations and untested
hypotheses. Include usable source references and identify calculations actually
run; supplied-but-unrun code remains unrun. Optional files supplement the report.

## Codex integration
Preserve the original once; inspect attachments before execution; check relevant
baseline differences. Reuse or update canonical claims and arguments. Record each
material finding's incorporated/open/refuted/duplicate/blocked disposition once,
grouping duplicates. A short sentence with links is enough for a single finding.
Do not silently drop an inconvenient result or accept an argument from fluency.

Include the receipt in the usual final reply: report location, canonical claim
and argument links, unresolved issue, actual validation and source/push status.
No separate receipt file, repeated full report, new mandatory session, or automatic
push. A local sandbox path or live-chat URL is not a durable repository reference.
